content.text: Each order-summary total displayed at checkout equals the corresponding cart total captured immediately before checkout.

expected_answer.operand: every order-summary total displayed at checkout equals the corresponding cart total captured immediately before checkout

content.text: Leaving checkout and returning within the same browser session preserves the basket contents captured at checkout entry.

expected_answer.baseline: basket contents captured at checkout entry
expected_answer.operand: the same basket contents are shown after leaving checkout and returning within the same browser session

content.text: Activating the checkout entry point from a non-empty cart opens checkout.

expected_answer.baseline: shopper is on the cart page with a non-empty basket

content.text: Checkout shows a guest checkout option to an anonymous shopper.
Checkout shows a register/login option to an anonymous shopper.
From a non-empty cart, the checkout entry point is visible.

expected_answer.operand: checkout entry point on the cart page

judgements.rationale: [risk_factors] Applied money because mismatched totals can misstate the payable amount, user-reach because every shopper entering checkout sees the summary, and change-frequency because cart and checkout totals commonly move with pricing, discount, and tax changes.

[risk_factors] Applied money because losing basket state breaks conversion, data-loss because the shopper's selected basket contents are the state at risk, user-reach because any shopper can navigate away and return, and change-frequency because basket/session persistence often changes with cart and checkout work.

[risk_factors] Applied money because unreachable checkout blocks purchase start, user-reach because every cart shopper depends on this transition, and change-frequency because entry routing and CTA behavior often change during storefront work.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because anonymous checkout entry affects a broad shopper population, and change-frequency because guest-flow presentation commonly changes with checkout experiments and account-entry updates.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because anonymous shoppers need the account-entry path at checkout, and change-frequency because sign-in and registration entry options are often revised together with checkout UX.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because the checkout control must be discoverable to proceed, and change-frequency because cart-page CTA layout and visibility rules often change during storefront updates.
